newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia state workers declare strike for February.
newsitem.headline: Colombia state workers declare strike for February.

text.p: Colombia's main public sector unions declared a nationwide strike beginning Feb. 11 involving about 800,000 state employees in key sectors of the economy, such as oil and telecommunications.

"Public sector workers will launch the strike on Feb. 11 with a single strike committee and a single negotiating committee to maintian solidarity. How long the action lasts depends on the government's willingness to negotiate," said Wislon Borja, head of the FENALTRASE public sector union.
The announcement of a national, indefinite strike came a week after President Ernesto Samper decreed a state of economic emergency to combat the yawning fiscal deficit.
Among the crisis measures already outlined are a broadening of the tax base, a cut in public spending and controls on contracting new foreign debt.
The unions fear cuts in the state payroll may be in the pipeline together with the imposition of value added tax on a range of hitherto untaxed basic foodstuffs.

State workers were given a weighted pay rise of 13.5 percent compared to a 1996 inflation rate of 21.63 percent. The government decreed a below-inflation 21.02 percent rise in the minimum wage, the point of reference for other wage hikes.

Colombia's main Pacific coast port of Buenaventura has been gripped by a dock workers' strike for the last six days, which has blocked 60 percent of the country's high-earning coffee exports and all its sugar exports.
Legal workers, including judges and magistrates, went out on strike on Monday and prison workers were threatening to strike if their demands for higher wages were not met.

Labor Minister Orlando Obregon said on Monday he would take steps to declare the legal workers' strike illegal and would do the same with the planned February strike if it affected essential services.
